quick: No data on use during pregnancy; give if clearly needed
Not expected to affect the breastfed infant
Observe for hypersensitivity; apnea risk in preterm infants
summary: PCV13 is a conjugate vaccine containing capsular polysaccharides of 13 pneumococcal serotypes conjugated to diphtheria CRM197 protein. It is given intramuscularly to prevent invasive pneumococcal disease and otitis media in infants/children and pneumococcal disease in adults. The conjugate format produces a T-cell-dependent response with immunologic memory, unlike plain polysaccharide vaccines.
indications: Active immunization for prevention of invasive disease caused by the 13 vaccine pneumococcal serotypes in infants and children 6 weeks through 17 years
Prevention of otitis media caused by vaccine serotypes in infants and children 6 weeks through 5 years
Active immunization for prevention of pneumonia and invasive pneumococcal disease in adults 18 years and older

dosage.n: Followed by a 4th (booster) dose at 12-15 months

dosage.d: 0.5 mL IM, number of doses by age at first dose

admin: Administer by intramuscular injection only (anterolateral thigh in infants, deltoid in older children/adults)
Do not inject intravenously, intradermally or subcutaneously
Shake the prefilled syringe well to obtain a homogeneous white suspension before use
Do not use if particulate matter or discoloration is present
Have epinephrine and resuscitation equipment available for anaphylaxis
moa: Each capsular polysaccharide is covalently conjugated to the non-toxic diphtheria CRM197 carrier protein. This converts the T-cell-independent polysaccharide response into a T-cell-dependent response, inducing functional anticapsular IgG antibodies and immunologic memory, including in young infants whose immune systems respond poorly to plain polysaccharides.

absolute: Severe allergic reaction (e.g., anaphylaxis) to any component of PCV13 or to any diphtheria toxoid-containing vaccine
relative: Moderate or severe acute illness with or without fever (defer until recovery)

preg: There are no adequate data on use in pregnant women. Administer to a pregnant woman only if clearly needed and after weighing benefit against risk.
lact: It is not known whether the vaccine antigens are excreted in human milk; PCV13 is not expected to cause harm to the breastfed infant.
renal: No dosage adjustment is required in renal impairment.
hepatic: No dosage adjustment is required in hepatic impairment.

moderate: Immunosuppressive therapy (corticosteroids, chemotherapy, radiation) may diminish the antibody response
minor: May be given concomitantly with other age-appropriate vaccines at separate injection sites
interactions.diagnostics: No significant interference with laboratory tests

common: Injection-site redness, swelling, pain or tenderness
emergency: Apnea with cyanosis in preterm infants

monitoring: Observe for at least 15-30 minutes after vaccination for hypersensitivity
Respiratory monitoring of very premature infants for 48-72 h after the primary series
Document lot number and vaccine in the immunization record
counsel: Mild fever, fussiness and soreness at the injection site are common and usually resolve within a couple of days
Use age-appropriate antipyretics if needed for fever or discomfort
Complete the full recommended schedule for best protection
The vaccine protects only against the 13 serotypes it contains, not all pneumococcal disease
Report any severe or unexpected reaction promptly
pk: Protective antibody levels develop over 1-2 weeks after dosing
Peak IgG response within weeks of completing the series
Not applicable (immune-mediated, not a small molecule)
Long-lasting protection with immunologic memory; boosters per schedule
Store refrigerated at 2-8 C; do not freeze; protect from light
pearls: Conjugation to CRM197 enables a protective response in infants under 2 years, unlike plain polysaccharide vaccine (PPSV23)
PCV13 also reduces nasopharyngeal carriage, providing herd protection
Adult immunocompromised patients often receive PCV13 followed by PPSV23 in a defined sequence
Do not freeze - freezing irreversibly damages the vaccine
Premature infants should still be vaccinated on schedule by chronological age, with apnea monitoring
missed: If a dose in a multi-dose schedule is delayed, give it as soon as possible and resume the recommended intervals; the series does not need to be restarted.
overdose: Overdose is unlikely with a single 0.5 mL dose; inadvertent extra doses are managed with reassurance and symptomatic care for local/systemic reactions.
